alt_text: One multi-layer-denominator graph first shows longitudinal WHOOP and Strava transport-context coverage, then episodic Kubios chest/body-frame body-coupling metrics, followed by persisted FSI and CSS context where available. Every accessible-table row carries its evidence-layer label and separate longitudinal, episodic-component, persisted-FSI, available-metric, and missing-event support. Fixed rail is shown only as an outlined planned comparator with no numeric value.

episodic_kubios_body_coupling.label: EPISODIC BODY-COUPLING / COMPONENT SUPPORT (Kubios + WHOOP + Strava)

source_systems: Kubios/Polar H10 episodic chest/body-frame metrics with linked WHOOP + Strava context

finding: Measured transportation cohorts have distinct mechanical and physiological distributions. Passive-passenger environments remain separate from the active-controlled motorcycle context and are not collapsed into one ranking.
functional_meaning: Body coupling preserves the difference between passive vehicle input and active locomotor control while making duration, coverage, and missing modalities auditable.
interpretation: Transportation profiles vary across passive-passenger and active-controlled contexts. Longitudinal context support is shown as coverage, while episodic Kubios body-coupling comparisons and persisted identities retain their own denominators.
limitation: Motorcycle is active transport and passenger modes are passive transport. Each evidence layer retains its own labeled denominator; unequal-n descriptive profiles do not rank modes as universally best or worst.
limitations: Sample counts, date coverage, source scope, missingness, and measurement availability accompany each scientific result.
long_description: Transportation profiles vary across passive-passenger and active-controlled contexts. Longitudinal context support is shown as coverage, while episodic Kubios body-coupling comparisons and persisted identities retain their own denominators. LONGITUDINAL CONTEXT SUPPORT (WHOOP + Strava) is context coverage, not the denominator for episodic body-coupling values. EPISODIC BODY-COUPLING / COMPONENT SUPPORT (Kubios + WHOOP + Strava) is shown beside chest/body-frame mechanical and physiologic comparisons. PERSISTED FSI SUPPORT is labeled separately where the persisted identity is displayed. SilverRide remains distinct from other sedan/taxi records. Motorcycle remains active controlled and is not interpreted as passive passenger exposure. Fixed rail is a planned, unmeasured comparator and has no numeric bar. N-of-1 case study example This N-of-1 case study example illustrates a review method and is not universal. Canonical case evidence: https://handicapskater.com/evidence/transportation/ Sample counts, date coverage, source scope, missingness, and measurement availability accompany each scientific result.
method_disclosure: This N-of-1 case study example illustrates a review method and is not universal.

planned_comparator.label: FIXED RAIL
planned_comparator.limitation: No direct fixed-rail mechanical or physiological measurement is currently available. Access history, legal argument, and scientific findings remain separate claim classes.
planned_comparator.research_question: How does fixed-rail body-coupling burden compare with ParaTransit bus, van, sedan, and other transportation environments using the same N-of-1 instrumentation?

qualifications: LONGITUDINAL CONTEXT SUPPORT (WHOOP + Strava) is context coverage, not the denominator for episodic body-coupling values.
EPISODIC BODY-COUPLING / COMPONENT SUPPORT (Kubios + WHOOP + Strava) is shown beside chest/body-frame mechanical and physiologic comparisons.
PERSISTED FSI SUPPORT is labeled separately where the persisted identity is displayed.
SilverRide remains distinct from other sedan/taxi records.
Motorcycle remains active controlled and is not interpreted as passive passenger exposure.
Fixed rail is a planned, unmeasured comparator and has no numeric bar.
This N-of-1 case study example illustrates a review method and is not universal.
question: How does measured body-coupling burden differ among transportation environments?
